inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K XBRL: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $257M (cash-flow add-back) plus $177M net cash tax withholding on award settlement (StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueShareBasedCompensation -177, i.e. withholding in excess of option proceeds). No combined figure published, so the two lines are summed. Withholding is elevated because awards granted at $70-170 vest with the stock at $500-1,000; that appreciated delivery value is the true cost to holders.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $3,316M; H1-2026 $3,671M against a $10B authorisation. The flat share count IS being funded in cash (basic count 275.9M at FY2024 -> 266.3M at 2026-06-30); repurchases are value-neutral here because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z regular close (Friday close; latest regular session before the 2026-09-28 valuation date; 52-week range 530.16-1195.94)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 266.33M basic shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~2.2M dilutive options/RSUs (Q2-2026 diluted 270M vs basic 268M weighted average). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; non-SBC issuance is nil (Prolec GE was paid in cash and debt, not shares).
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q2-2026 10-Q: LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsIncludingCurrentMaturities $2,849M (of which ~$2,567M is the February 2026 Prolec GE acquisition notes) less cash of $12,740M = $13,120M cash, equivalents and restricted cash at 2026-06-30 less ~$380M restricted cash (FY2025 restricted balance $379M carried, Q2 figure not separately tagged). Operating lease liabilities ($871M) are EXCLUDED: under US GAAP operating-lease cost sits inside operating expense/EBITDA (treatment B), so charging them again as debt would double-count. Finance leases are inside the $2,849M.
inputs.net_cash_caveat: The ~$9.9B net cash is substantially customer advances: contract liabilities rose from $17.7B (FY2024) to $26.0B (FY2025) to $40.0B (2026-06-30). Those advances will be consumed as the backlog is executed (costs incurred against revenue already collected). The model adds the cash at face but deliberately does NOT capitalise the advance inflow: wc_capture is held at 10% of the revenue change in base (not the 200%+ realised in FY2025-H1 2026) and goes negative in bear. This is the single biggest judgment in the file and the reason the model's owner FCF sits far below the company's $11.5-12.5B FY2026 reported-FCF guidance.
inputs.interest_income_basis: ESTIMATE. GEV reports 'interest and other financial charges - net' as one line and tags no separate interest-income element. Average FY2025 cash ~$8.3B ($8,205M -> $8,848M) at ~3% money-market yield ~= $250M; interest paid was $53M (InterestPaidNet). Stripped because net cash (~$9.9B) exceeds the owner-FCF base (~$3B) by >3x, so leaving it in the flows would count the cash pile twice.
inputs.one_offs_excluded: FY2025 net income $4,884M includes a ~$2.9B non-cash US deferred-tax valuation-allowance release (DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance $8,420M -> $4,816M; IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit -$2,051M). Q1-2026 net income $4,750M includes a ~$4.5B pre-tax non-cash step-acquisition remeasurement gain on the previously equity-accounted 50% of Prolec GE (OtherNonoperatingIncomeExpense $4,762M in Q1-2026 vs $119M in Q1-2025). Neither touches the model: the build starts from revenue and an EBITDA margin path anchored to GAAP operating income + D&A + restructuring (FY2025: $1,388M + $853M + $285M = $2,526M, 6.6%), not from net income. The Prolec GE acquisition itself IS in the model as a permanent change: ~$3B of consolidated transformer revenue inside the FY2026 growth step, the $2,567M acquisition notes inside total debt, the $4,885M cash paid already out of the Q2-2026 cash balance, and the intangibles amortisation inside the higher D&A path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10-yr UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.2 (high-volatility large cap, 52-week range 530-1196) = ~10.2% cost of equity; debt is <2% of enterprise value at ~5% pre-tax, so WACC rounds to 9.5%. Same rate in all three scenarios: cyclicality, hyperscaler concentration and offshore-wind execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): operating-lease cost is inside EBITDA under US GAAP, so operating lease liabilities ($871M at 2026-06-30) are excluded from net debt. Finance leases ($<100M) are within total_debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests of $1,158M (2026-06-30) are deducted once, in the equity bridge. NCI's share of net income is ~nil (-$4M FY2025, -$15M H1-2026), so the flows are effectively attributable already; deducting the book stock is a small (~$4/share) conservatism rather than a double charge.
inputs.excluded_income_matching_assets: Equity-method income ($269M FY2025, mostly the pre-acquisition Prolec GE 50% share; ~$70M run-rate post-acquisition) sits below operating income and is NOT in the EBITDA path, so the remaining equity-method investments ($1,384M at 2026-06-30, book) are added in the bridge. Non-operating benefit (pension/OPEB) income (~$590M FY2025, non-cash) is likewise excluded from EBITDA; the principal plans showed a net pension ASSET of $1,163M at FY2025 (DefinedBenefitPlanAssetsForPlanBenefitsNoncurrent), so no deficit is deducted and no asset is added.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials'), read with owner-fcf.md and owner-fcf-adaptations.md (leases, NCI, matching-asset rule, charge-risk-once). Fresh build, no prior DCF, no memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 (last audited year); year 1 = FY2026 at the Q2-2026 guidance midpoint ($45.5-46.5B revenue, 12-14% adjusted EBITDA margin). Balance sheet and share count are from the 2026-06-30 10-Q, which is more recent than FY0: roughly half a year of FY2026 operating owner-FCF (~$1.5-2B, <1% of value) is therefore both inside the cash balance and inside year 1; offset by discounting FY2026 a full period from a September valuation date. Ten-year horizon because the EBITDA margin is still ramping (6.6% FY2025 -> guided 12-14% FY2026 -> 15.5% mature in base). Terminal value capped at 16x (base) / 18x (bull) / 12x (bear) year-10 owner FCF, the cyclical-industrial band; Gordon at 9.5%/3.0% is 15.8x so the base cap barely binds. Price is the Friday 2026-09-25 regular close, not after-hours.

equity_bridge.item: Equity-method investments at book (income excluded from flows)
equity_bridge.note: Q2-2026 10-Q EquityMethodInvestments $1,384M; matching-asset rule for the excluded equity income
Q2-2026 10-Q MinorityInterest $1,158M; charged once, here, not in the flows

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (1.9%, FY2022 $11,607M -> FY2025 $12,296M) diverges >30% from revenue 3-yr CAGR (8.7%, $29,654M -> $38,068M). Equity is depressed by $3.4B of FY2024-25 buybacks and the pre-spin losses, and inflated by the FY2025 $2.9B valuation-allowance release; it is not a growth signal for this company.
historical_growth.notes: History only runs FY2022-FY2025 (carve-out financials pre-April-2024 spin-off), so no 5-year CAGRs exist. EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined from negative bases (FY2022 EPS -$10.00, FCF -$627M; FY2023 EPS -$1.60). Owner FCF: FY2024 $1,700M reported - $155M SBC - ~$200M interest = ~$1,345M; FY2025 $3,710M - $434M - $250M = $3,026M. The FY2025 figure itself is flattered by an $8.2B rise in contract liabilities (customer advances), so the 125% one-year owner-FCF growth is not a run-rate. selected_growth_rate is the base scenario's FY2025-FY2030 revenue CAGR (11.3%), the only series that describes the post-spin, post-Prolec business.

base.growth_note: Y1 +21% = FY2026 guidance midpoint $46.0B ($45.5-46.5B), of which ~$3B is the consolidated Prolec GE transformer business (11 months) and ~13% is organic. Y2-Y4 10-12% -> 8%: backlog $176B heading to ~$200B by 2027 and gas-turbine slots sold into 2029-30 give multi-year visibility; decay to 3% by year 9 as the AI/data-centre build plateaus.
base.margin_note: FY2025 cash-operating EBITDA (GAAP operating income + D&A + restructuring) was 6.6%. Y1 12.0% sits at the bottom of the company's 12-14% adjusted-EBITDA guidance because the company measure adds back separation costs and Prolec purchase-accounting charges that are real cash in 2026. Ramps to 15.5% by year 5 (Power services mix, Prolec accretion, offshore-wind losses fading) and holds: above the company's 2028 target band, below what a pure services annuity would earn.
base.wc_note: 10% of the YoY revenue change. Contract liabilities rose $8.2B in FY2025 and $14.1B in H1-2026 (200%+ of the revenue change) as customers prepaid for scarce turbine and transformer slots; the model capitalises only a normal long-cycle advance ratio and lets the FY2025-26 windfall sit in the balance-sheet cash where it already is.
base.tax_note: Cash taxes: FY2025 $830M on ~$2.5B cash EBIT (~30% incl. foreign taxes while US was loss-making); H1-2026 $1,258M. 24% Y1 then 23% blended statutory. The $5.8B net DTA (US NOLs post valuation-allowance release) will shelter US cash tax for some years; that shelter is NOT modelled, which is conservative by perhaps $2-3/share per year of shelter.

bull.narrative: Supercycle is structural: backlog passes $200B in 2027 and keeps growing, gas-turbine pricing holds, Electrification (Prolec + grid) compounds at data-centre pace, offshore wind is wound down without further charges, SMRs add a leg late in the decade. EBITDA reaches 18% (top of the company's long-range ambition) and advances keep funding 25% of growth.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance (backlog is contracted) but the cycle rolls over from 2027: hyperscaler capex decelerates, slot reservations are deferred or cancelled, and revenue flattens then dips in 2029-30 as the 2025-26 order surge is delivered without replacement. Margins stall at 11-12% (wind charges, tariff and input-cost inflation on fixed-price backlog, Vineyard Wind litigation). Customer advances unwind: working capital consumes cash as contract liabilities shrink toward a normal ratio, so the net cash pile is partly spent delivering already-collected orders.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 at the raised guidance midpoint ($46.0B, 12% cash-operating EBITDA margin) with Prolec GE consolidated, then 10-12% growth through 2028 as the $176-200B backlog converts, fading to 3% by 2034. Margin ramps to 15.5% by 2030 on Power services mix, Electrification scale and shrinking offshore-wind losses, and holds. Customer advances are treated as a balance-sheet stock, not a recurring flow: only 10% of each year's revenue increase is captured as working-capital inflow. Terminal at 16x year-10 owner FCF (Gordon 9.5%/3.0% = 15.8x).
scenario_narratives.bull: Structural AI/electrification demand: revenue compounds at 15-13-11% through 2029, Electrification and Prolec transformers scale into a durable grid-equipment franchise, gas-turbine pricing power persists, offshore wind is exited cleanly, and margins reach 18% by 2031. Advances fund 25% of growth. Terminal 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2025-26 order surge proves to be a cyclical peak: growth stalls from 2027, revenue dips in 2029-30, margins stay at 11-12% under wind, tariff and fixed-price-backlog pressure, and the advance-funded cash is consumed delivering already-collected orders (negative working-capital capture). Terminal 12x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the thesis rests on one driver — hyperscaler power capex staying at 2025-26 intensity for the rest of the decade — and because ~$40B of customer advances make the cash position reversible in a downturn. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things at once: the supercycle lasting beyond 2028, margins reaching 18% and offshore wind exiting without further charges. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value GE Vernova on the cash the operating business earns — GAAP operating income + D&A, less SBC, cash tax, capex and a normal working-capital ratio — not on reported net income (distorted by the FY2025 $2.9B valuation-allowance release and the Q1-2026 $4.5B Prolec GE remeasurement gain) and not on reported FCF (FY2026 guidance of $11.5-12.5B is roughly half customer advances on a backlog the company has yet to build). The model gives full credit for the $9.9B net cash those advances have created, gives permanent credit for Prolec GE as a consolidated business with its acquisition debt, and lets margins ramp well past today's levels. The gap between the resulting value and the market price is therefore a statement about one thing: the price capitalises the advance-driven FCF as if it recurs, and assumes the AI power supercycle both persists and expands margins beyond anything the company has guided.
key_risks_to_valuation: Customer advances: $40B of contract liabilities at 2026-06-30 fund most of the net cash; if order intake slows, working capital reverses and the cash pile is spent delivering the backlog (bear scenario captures this with negative wc_capture).
Hyperscaler concentration: incremental gas-turbine and Electrification orders depend on a handful of AI data-centre capex decisions.
Offshore wind: Vineyard Wind litigation and Dogger Bank losses could produce further charges not in the margin path.
Fixed-price long-cycle backlog exposed to tariffs, steel/copper and electrical-steel inflation through 2029-30.
Margin path to 15.5% (base) / 18% (bull) is above anything achieved to date (6.6% FY2025 cash-operating basis); execution on the ramp is the main upside-risk lever.
Interest income is an estimate ($250M) and the US NOL cash-tax shelter is unmodelled; both are small and pull in opposite directions.
Terminal value is ~55-60% of enterprise value in every scenario; the cyclical cap (16x/18x/12x) is the main lever on the answer.
